contains one of at most $7|Y'|_M$ cubes consisting of
its cubes and their face neighbors. Since
$|Z|_M\le c_X(d_M(Z)+1)\le\kappa_0(d_M(Z)+1)$ and
$a^q\le q!\exp(a)$, the counting estimate gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{Z\text{ incompatible with }Y'}
      \exp(-2\kappa_0d_M(Z))|Z|_M^{q}
            &\le7q!\exp(\kappa_0)K_{\mathrm{pol}}|Y'|_M,\\
 \sum_{Z\subseteq Y}\exp(-2\kappa_0d_M(Z))|Z|_M^q
            &\le q!\exp(\kappa_0)K_{\mathrm{pol}}|Y|_M.
\end{align*}
Summing from leaves to root thus costs at most
$(7\exp(\kappa_0)K_{\mathrm{pol}})^n|Y|_M\prod_jq_j!$.
For prescribed children counts, Cayley's degree formula
\cite[Prop.~4]{PostnikovLin2019}
counts
$(n-2)!/((q_1-1)!\prod_{j\ge2}q_j!)$ trees, where
$q_1\ge1$ and $\sum_jq_j=n-1$.
Consequently
\[
 \sum_{\text{trees}}\prod_jq_j!
   =(n-2)!\sum_{(q_j)}q_1
   \le(n-1)!\binom{2n-2}{n-1}
   \le(n-1)!4^{n-1}.
\]
Collecting the factors, also for $n=1$, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-connected-n-bound}
 \frac{S_n(Y)}{n!}
 \le7H_1\exp(\kappa_0)K_{\mathrm{pol}}|Y|_M
                                      \exp(-a_6d_M(Y))z_S^{n-1}.
\end{equation}
Since $z_S\le1/2$, sum the geometric series and use
$|Y|_M\le c_X\exp(d_M(Y))$ and $a_6-1=a_3$.
The bound becomes
\[
 98c_X^2K_{\mathrm{pol}}^2\exp(\kappa_0+3a_5)
                                 H_{\mathrm{cl}}\exp(-a_3d_M(Y))
 \le c_S'H_{\mathrm{cl}}\exp(-a_3d_M(Y)),
\]
because $\kappa_0+3a_5=3\kappa-8\kappa_0-6$.
Summing only $n>N$ gives the additional factor $2^{-N}$.
This proves absolute convergence and the claimed estimates.

It remains to justify the logarithm identity after
substitution in \eqref{eq:rgnl-connected-graph-identity}.
The even subalgebra with the coefficient norm is a
commutative Banach algebra, and the polymer set is finite.
By \eqref{eq:rgnl-connected-n-bound}, the connected norm sum is finite,
and the norm sum of products in its exponential is at most its exponential.
Absolute regrouping by the formal $z_Y$ monomials is therefore valid.
Their coefficients are those of \eqref{eq:rgnl-connected-graph-identity};
substitute $z_Y=H(Y)$ to obtain \eqref{eq:rgnl-compatible-partition},
then group by union to obtain \eqref{eq:rgnl-log-identity}.
\end{proof}

There are also polynomial approximants to this logarithm
which converge uniformly for all families satisfying the
preceding bound, at fixed side. Replace $\exp V-1$ by
$p_N(V)=\sum_{1\le j\le N}V^j/j!$ in $K,H$, and stop
the connected series at $n=N$; denote the result $E_N^\#$.
It is a polynomial in integrals of products of $V(X_i)$,
$X_i\subseteq Y$, and has the same bound
\eqref{eq:rgnl-log-bound}. To verify uniform convergence,
write $D=|\mathcal P_k|$. Since $\|V(X)\|\le1$,
\[
 \|\exp V(X)-1-p_N(V(X))\|
                                  \le\frac{\exp(1)}{(N+1)!}.
\]
Telescoping each finite product in $K$ gives
\[
 \|H(Y)-H_N(Y)\|\le
                             \frac{4^DD\exp(1)}{(N+1)!}.
\]
Thus this difference is at most $\delta_N\mu(Y)$, where
\[
 \delta_N=\frac{4^DD\exp(1)}
                      {(N+1)!\min_{Y\in\mathcal P_k}\mu(Y)}
                                                   \longrightarrow0.
\]
Replacing the $n$ factors in a connected term costs at
most $n\delta_N\prod_i\mu(Y_i)$. Summing
\eqref{eq:rgnl-connected-n-bound} with this factor, using
$\sum_{n\ge1}n2^{-(n-1)}=4$, and adding the tail yields
\[
 \sup_Y\|E^\#(Y)-E_N^\#(Y)\|
 \le28\delta_NH_1\exp(\kappa_0)K_{\mathrm{pol}}(\ell/M)^3
                                  +2^{-N}c_S'H_{\mathrm{cl}}.
\]
This convergence is uniform in the connections and the
allowed data. The displayed error depends on the side;
no volume-independent approximation is claimed.

\subsubsection{Symmetries of the local logarithm}
\label{subsec:rgnl-symmetries}

Apply Prop.~\ref{prop:rgnl-cluster-logarithm} with $V=F$,
$w=h/4$, and denote its output by $E_k^\#(m,\mathscr E)$.
Products on subpolymers of $Y$ preserve the leg supports, local
connection dependence, and dependence only on $m'$ and
$\mathscr E^r(X)$ for $X\subseteq Y$. The norm bound and uniform
polynomial approximants give analytic connection coefficients.
We next carry the symmetries through these finite operations,
integration and the convergent logarithm.

Let $\mathbb G_k^L$ denote the chamber symmetry group with
translations in $LM\Z^3$, so that it preserves every
parameter partition. Its actions and the gauge,
charge-conjugation and reality actions are those of
\S~\ref{subsec:rg-activity-spaces}.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rgnl-symmetries}
The local logarithm satisfies
\begin{align}
 a_{\tilde g}E_k^\#(\tilde gY;\tilde gA,\tilde g\mathscr C)
          &=E_k^\#(Y;A,\mathscr C),\qquad \tilde g\in\mathbb G_k^L,
                                      \label{eq:rgnl-lattice-symmetry}\\
 G_{\lambda+\lambda'}E_k^\#(Y;A^1,\mathscr C^1)
          &=E_k^\#(Y;A,\mathscr C),    \label{eq:rgnl-gauge-symmetry}\\
 \mathrm{Cg}\,E_k^\#(Y;-A,-\mathscr C)
          &=E_k^\#(Y;A,\mathscr C).    \label{eq:rgnl-charge-symmetry}
\end{align}
In the gauge identity both pairs belong to the domain and
 $A^1=A-d\lambda$, $\mathscr C^1=\mathscr C-d\lambda'$
on all bonds at distance at most $1$ from $Y$, with
real $\lambda,\lambda'$. Here $d\lambda$ denotes the
lattice gradient, as in the preceding gauge conventions.
For real $m$ and $\mathscr E\in K_k^x$ one also has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-reality-symmetry}
 \mathbf K E_k^\#(Y;-\overline A,-\overline{\mathscr C})
                                        =E_k^\#(Y;A,\mathscr C).
\end{equation}
Every monomial is balanced.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The four actions are continuous ring automorphisms, linear except for
$\mathbf K$. Equivariant substitutions commute with them on generators,
hence on the algebra. Real finite differences
\eqref{eq:rgnl-finite-difference} also commute. Lattice actions permute
parameter cubes and localization terms, preserving connectedness,
incidences and Ursell coefficients.

The contour functional commutes with the linear actions.
For the antilinear action, parametrize $t=r\exp(i\theta)$:
\[
 \mathcal C_rf=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
             \frac{f(r\exp(i\theta))}{r\exp(i\theta)-1}\,\dd\theta.
\]
Conjugating coefficients and replacing $\theta$ by $-\theta$ leaves
this contour functional unchanged at the transformed arguments.
Wick pairings are real and invariant under
$W\mapsto UW$, $\bar W\mapsto(U^{-1})^T\bar W$,
so integration commutes with these linear or antilinear changes.
This covers lattice and gauge actions, $\mathbf K$ with $U=\varkappa$,
and charge extended as the identity on $W$; the last case needs the
separate covariance argument below.

For a lattice symmetry the primitive covariance gives
\[
 Z(\tilde gs')[\tilde g\zeta]=\tilde gZ(s')[\zeta],\qquad
 H_k(\tilde gs'',\tilde gB)\tilde g=\tilde gH_k(s'',B),
 \qquad
 \Gamma_k(\tilde gs'',\tilde gB)\tilde g=\tilde g\Gamma_k(s'',B).
\]
The barred action follows from
$(S^{-1})^T=\pm\mathsf C^{-1}S\mathsf C$.
Transported endpoints give covariance of the H\"older quotients, hence
of $J_k^\#\Psi,W_k^\#$. The primitive relation
$M_k(\tilde gX,\tilde gB)=\tilde gM_k(X,B)\tilde g^{-1}$,
change of chamber/spin indices, incoming symmetry, and
\eqref{eq:rg-step-substitution-covariances} give invariance of the
bilinear, mass, activity and reconstruction terms. The photon box measure
is invariant. The preceding commutation rules through both localizations,
integration and the connected series prove \eqref{eq:rgnl-lattice-symmetry}.

For the gauge identity set $\Lambda=\lambda+\lambda'$.
In a summand assigned to $Y$, all parameters outside $Y$
vanish. The local row result proves that $B^1$ may be
replaced by $B-d\Lambda$ in every row used in that
summand. The latter field is still in the operator domain,
since real gauge shifts preserve it.
Telescoping the gradient along each path gives
\[
 U_{B-d\Lambda}(x,x')
       =U_B(x,x')\exp\big(-ie(\Lambda(c')-\Lambda(c))\big).
\]
The ordinary primitive row obeys
\[
 H_k(s'',B^1)(x,\cdot)
       =\exp(ie\Lambda(c))H_k(s'',B)(x,\cdot)
                                                 \exp(-ie\Lambda^u),
\]
when it is nonzero, where $\Lambda^u$ is the function
on the unit indices. The barred row has the inverse
phases. In the H\"older row the phase at its second
point cancels that from the transport, leaving exactly
$\exp(ie\Lambda(c))$, the phase of the first point.
The row of $\Gamma_k$ has the corresponding two-sided
gauge covariance. Its composition with $H_k^\#$ thus
gives the same covariance for $W_k^\#$, including the
rows which vanish outside $Y$.
The primitive bilinear and the local mass form are
gauge invariant, and so is $R\mathscr E$ under the
separate shifts of its two connection arguments. The reconstruction
substitution also commutes with this local gauge action.
The photon fields and photon measure are unchanged.
The finite operations and integration therefore prove
\eqref{eq:rgnl-gauge-symmetry}.

For reality, the photon primitives are real on real
parameter families. Their analytic dependence extends
this identity to
$\overline{O(\bar s')}=O(s')$ on the full polydisc.
Since $C$ is real,
\[
 Z(\bar s')[-\zeta]=-\overline{Z(s')[\zeta]}.
\]
Transform $s\mapsto\bar s$, $t\mapsto\bar t$,
$\zeta\mapsto-\zeta$ and
$(A,\mathscr C)\mapsto(-\bar A,-\overline{\mathscr C})$.
The fermion identities are
\[
 \overline{H_k(\bar s'',-\bar B)}
                         =\varkappa^{-1}H_k(s'',B)\varkappa,\qquad
 \overline{\Gamma_k(\bar s'',-\bar B)}
                         =\varkappa^{-1}\Gamma_k(s'',B)\varkappa.
\]
For the barred field use
$\varkappa\mathsf C=-\mathsf C\varkappa$.
The transport relation
$\overline{U_{-\bar B}(x,x')}=U_B(x,x')$
then gives the same identities for the H\"older rows.
The local quadratic primitive obeys the corresponding
identity, and $\varkappa^T\varkappa=1$ preserves the
mass form. The number $m'$ is real for the present data,
and $R\mathscr E$ and the reconstruction substitution
have the reality symmetry. The contour argument just
given, invariance of the box under sign reversal, and
weighted integration prove
\eqref{eq:rgnl-reality-symmetry}.

Charge conjugation gives the first-localization symmetry
by
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 H_k(s'',-B)\mathsf C=\mathsf C\bar H_k(s'',B),\qquad
 \bar H_k(s'',-B)\mathsf C=\mathsf C H_k(s'',B),\\
 M_k(X,-B)^T=\mathsf C^{-1}M_k(X,B)\mathsf C .
 \end{gathered}
\]
Anticommuting the two transformed legs verifies the
bilinear and mass-form identities. The first-step
vertex has this symmetry by its explicit two-half formula.
It follows that
\[
 \mathrm{Cg}\,E_{\le3}(X;-A,-\mathscr C,-\zeta)
                                        =E_{\le3}(X;A,\mathscr C,\zeta).
\]
Direct covariance of the second substitution is not
available, since its unbarred and barred fluctuations
use different factors. We instead compare their Wick
covariances.

Introduce independent generators $\phi^\#$ indexed like
$\psi^\#$, with their own charge-conjugation action,
and let $\operatorname{ad}$ add them to the old generators.
Put
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal V(X)
   ={}&\operatorname{ad}E_{\le3}(X)
      +\operatorname{ad}\mathscr E^r(X)-\mathscr E^r(X)\\
     &-\mathbf1_{X=\square}m'
          \big(\operatorname{ad}
                         \langle\bar\psi,\psi\rangle_\square
                                -\langle\bar\psi,\psi\rangle_\square\big).
\end{align*}
It has charge-conjugation symmetry under
$(A,\mathscr C,\zeta)\mapsto(-A,-\mathscr C,-\zeta)$.
Let $I_{s'',B}$ fix the old generators and replace
$\phi^\#$ by $W_k^\#(s'',B)$. The second-localization
input is exactly $I_{s'',B}\mathcal V(X)$, since
the polynomial contours in $G_4,G_5$ give their value
at $1$ minus their value at $0$.
For any union $U$, interpolation restricted to cubes
of $U$, with the disconnected terms removed, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-subvolume-substitution}
 \sum_{Y\subseteq U}F(Y)=
                        I_{\mathbf1_U,B}\sum_{X\subseteq U}\mathcal V(X).
\end{equation}

At $s''=\mathbf1_U$ define
\[
 \phi_\pm=H_k(\mathbf1_U,\pm B)\Gamma_k(\mathbf1_U,\pm B)W,
 \qquad
 \bar\phi_\pm=\bar H_k(\mathbf1_U,\pm B)\bar W,
 \qquad
 \phi'=\mathsf C\bar\phi_-,\quad
 \bar\phi'=\mathsf C^{-1}\phi_-.
\]
The substitution by $(\phi',\bar\phi')$ and their
H\"older quotients, denoted $I'$, satisfies
$\mathrm{Cg}\,I_{\mathbf1_U,-B}=I'\mathrm{Cg}$
on every generator, when $\mathrm{Cg}$ fixes $W$.
The only nonzero ordinary pair expectations for the
positive substitution are the kernel of
\[
 \mathcal G_U(B)
        =H_k(\mathbf1_U,B)\Gamma_k(\mathbf1_U,B)
                                            \bar H_k(\mathbf1_U,B)^T.
\]
The identity moment has kernel
$\mathbf1_{u=u'}/\nu(u)$, with $\nu=1/48$ at zero.
This precisely cancels one of the two measures in
the kernel composition, so the same formula holds
at every level. The primitive transpose relation gives
\[
 \mathcal G_U(-B)^T
                      =-\mathsf C^{-1}\mathcal G_U(B)\mathsf C^{-1}.
\]
Anticommuting $\bar\phi_-$ and $\phi_-$ therefore gives
\[
 \int\dd\mu_I(W)\,\phi'(x)\bar\phi'(x')^T
     =\mathsf C[-\mathcal G_U(-B)^T(x,x')]\mathsf C
     =\mathcal G_U(B)(x,x').
\]
Same-bar pair expectations vanish in both substitutions.
The pair generators are obtained by the identical
linear H\"older maps at $B,-B$, so their pair expectations
also agree. Wick's theorem now proves
$\int\dd\mu_I(W)I'Q=\int\dd\mu_I(W)I_{\mathbf1_U,B}Q$
for every polynomial $Q$ in the old and $\phi^\#$
generators: each monomial integral is the Pfaffian of
its pair expectations, with old generators as coefficients.

Apply this equality to the exponential of
$\sum_{X\subseteq U}\mathcal V(X)$ and use
$\zeta\mapsto-\zeta$. By
\eqref{eq:rgnl-subvolume-substitution}, the integrated
subvolume expression
$\Xi_U=\int\dd\mu_I(W)\dd\widehat\mu(\zeta)
\exp(\sum_{Y\subseteq U}F(Y))$
has charge-conjugation symmetry.
But $\Xi_U=\sum_{Z\subseteq U}H(Z)$, by the finite
Mayer expansion. Inverting this finite subset sum gives
\[
 H(Z)=\sum_{U\subseteq Z}(-1)^{|Z\setminus U|_M}\Xi_U.
\]
Thus each $H(Z)$ has the symmetry, and the real
coefficients and absolute convergence of the connected
series prove \eqref{eq:rgnl-charge-symmetry}.

Finally take a constant $\lambda$ and $\lambda'=0$
in \eqref{eq:rgnl-gauge-symmetry}. A monomial with
$n_u$ unbarred and $n_b$ barred legs acquires the factor
$\exp(ie\lambda(n_u-n_b))$. Invariance for every real
$\lambda$ and independence of the basis monomials force
its coefficient to vanish unless $n_u=n_b$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The scaled correction}
\label{subsec:rgnl-scaled-correction}

Let $S_L$ be the field scaling of
\eqref{eq:rg-leg-scaling}. The nonlinear correction is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-scaled-correction}
 E_k^*(m,\mathscr E)(Y;\mathscr A,\mathscr C)
  =\sum_{\bar X^L=LY}S_L
        E_k^\#(m,\mathscr E)(X;\mathscr A_L,\mathscr C_L).
\end{equation}
The correction $E_k^*$ is obtained by field scaling and
reblocking $E_k^\#$. The separate term
$\mathcal L(R\mathscr E)^{\mathrm{nat}}$ in the full step
carries the quadratic adjustment of the input activity.
The domain inclusions
\eqref{eq:rg-scaled-domain-inclusion} ensure
$(\mathscr A_L,\mathscr C_L)
\in\widetilde R_k^-\times\mathfrak X_k$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rgnl-scaled-correction}
For $(m,\mathscr E)\in\operatorname{Ball}_k^x(4)$,
\[
 E_k^*(m,\mathscr E)\in K_{k+1}^{x,\C},\qquad
                  \|E_k^*(m,\mathscr E)\|_{k+1}^x
                                      \le e^{1/4-6\varepsilon}.
\]
For real data its value belongs to $K_{k+1}^x$.
For two data in $\operatorname{Ball}_k^x(1)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-coupling-Lipschitz}
 \|E_k^*(m_1,\mathscr E_1)-E_k^*(m_2,\mathscr E_2)\|_{k+1}^x
 \le e^{1/4-6\varepsilon}
       \left(\frac{|m_1-m_2|}{w_k^{\mathrm m}}
              +\frac{\|\mathscr E_1-\mathscr E_2\|_k^x}
                                                    {w_k^{\mathrm E}}\right).
\end{equation}
The second quotient is absent at $k=0$.
Restriction to $\mathscr C=0$ gives the one-connection correction
formed from $(m,\mathscr E|_0)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The scaling identity gives
\[
 \|S_LQ\|_{h_{k+1}}
   =\|Q\|_{(L^{-1}h_{k+1,1},L^{-1-\alpha}h_{k+1,2})}
   \le\|Q\|_{h_k/4},
\]
since $h_{k+1,1}=L^{-1/8}h_{k,1}$,
$h_{k+1,2}=L^{-1/8+\varepsilon/2}h_{k,2}$ and $L\ge4$.
The polymer sum in \eqref{eq:rgnl-scaled-correction}
uses $Ld_M(Y)\le d_M(X)$ and $X\subseteq LY$.
Splitting $a_3=(a_3-\kappa_0)+\kappa_0$ therefore yields
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{\bar X^L=LY}\exp(-a_3d_M(X))
  &\le \exp(-L(a_3-\kappa_0)d_M(Y))
                         \sum_{X\subseteq LY}\exp(-\kappa_0d_M(X))\\
  &\le c_XK_{\mathrm{pol}}L^3
                  \exp(-[L(\kappa-6\kappa_0-4)-1]d_M(Y))\\
  &\le c_XK_{\mathrm{pol}}L^3\exp(-\kappa d_M(Y)).
\end{align*}
Together with \eqref{eq:rgnl-log-bound} this gives
\[
 \|E_k^*\|_{k+1}^x
  \le c_XK_{\mathrm{pol}}L^3c_S'H_{\mathrm{cl}}
  =504c_X^5K_{\mathrm{pol}}^5\exp(3\kappa)L^3e^{1/4-5\varepsilon}
  \le e^{1/4-6\varepsilon},
\]
using $c_SL^3e^\varepsilon\le1$.

Ordinary sites scale into $Y$, pair paths to scaled paths,
and $(x,x^{(3)})$ to $(x/L,(x/L)^{(3)})$. This preserves
admissibility, including intracluster pairs. The bonds meeting $X$
on which the coefficients depend scale to bonds meeting $Y$;
the scaled-domain inclusion gives analytic kernels.
The map $(S,a)\mapsto(S,a/L)$ identifies the lattice actions.
For gauges, $\Lambda_L(c)=L^{1/2}\Lambda(c/L)$ and
$(d\Lambda)_L=d\Lambda_L$, and the scaled neighborhoods on which
the kernels depend are contained in the stipulated unit neighborhood. Charge and reality commute with
the real scaling. Prop.~\ref{prop:rgnl-symmetries} therefore gives
$K_{k+1}^{x,\C}$ membership and its real subspace for real data.

For two unit-ball data $u_1,u_2$, put $B=e^{1/4-6\varepsilon}$ and
\[
 D=\max\left\{\frac{|m_1-m_2|}{w_k^{\mathrm m}},
          \frac{\|\mathscr E_1-\mathscr E_2\|_k^x}{w_k^{\mathrm E}}\right\},
\]
omitting the second entry at $k=0$. If $D=0$ the outputs agree.
Otherwise $D\le2$; set $r=3/D$,
$u(t)=u_2+t(u_1-u_2)$ and $f(t)=E_k^*(u(t))$.
For $|t|\le r$ the data norm is at most $1+rD=4$, so
$\|f(t)\|_{k+1}^x\le B$.
Since $F$ is affine in the data, the previously constructed polynomial
approximants, reblocked by \eqref{eq:rgnl-scaled-correction},
are polynomials $f_N(t)$ converging uniformly in activity norm on this disk.
Interpolation at finitely many distinct points gives their coefficients
finite activity norm. Coefficientwise Cauchy and Tonelli therefore give
\[
 f_N(1)-f_N(0)
   =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{|t|=r}\frac{f_N(t)}{t(t-1)}\,\dd t,\qquad
 \|f_N(1)-f_N(0)\|_{k+1}^x
   \le\frac{\sup_{|t|=r}\|f_N(t)\|_{k+1}^x}{r-1}.
\]
Passing to the uniform norm limit yields
\[
 \|E_k^*(u_1)-E_k^*(u_2)\|_{k+1}^x
 \le\frac B{r-1}=\frac{BD}{3-D}\le BD
 \le B\left(\frac{|m_1-m_2|}{w_k^{\mathrm m}}
       +\frac{\|\mathscr E_1-\mathscr E_2\|_k^x}{w_k^{\mathrm E}}\right).
\]
This is \eqref{eq:rgnl-coupling-Lipschitz}, with the activity quotient
again omitted at $k=0$.

Restriction commutes with extraction,
$m(\mathscr E)=m(\mathscr E|_0)$ and
$(R\mathscr E)|_0=R(\mathscr E|_0)$. Fermions use $A+\mathscr C$,
while photons and measures do not use $\mathscr C$.
Thus setting $\mathscr C=0$ gives exactly the finite expressions,
connected series and scaled correction for the activity
$\mathscr E|_0$, analytic in $A$ alone.
\end{proof}

The correction introduces only scaled incoming pair indices and
scaled type-$3$ pairs: $G_2,G_4$ only add fields at existing pair indices,
the mass contours have none, and reconstruction and the first vertex
introduce only $(x,x^{(3)})$. Sums, products and integrals preserve this list.
At zero only the latter pairs occur, of length $\eta_1$.

\subsubsection{The step identity and bounds}
\label{subsec:rgnl-current-step}

For the local determinant terms of
Prop.~\ref{prop:local-determinant-expansion}, put
\[
 \delta E_k^{\mathrm{det}}(X;\mathscr A,\mathscr C)
       =E_k^d(X,\mathscr A+\mathscr C)-E_k^d(X,\mathscr C),
 \qquad
 E_k^{\mathrm{det}}(X,\mathscr C)
       =E_k^d(X,\mathscr C)-E_k^d(X,0).
\]
These are scalar activities. With reblocking $\mathcal L$ from
\eqref{eq:rg-reblocking-definition}, the new activity has three
contributions: the normalized input, the determinant correction,
and the fluctuation correction $E_k^*$. Define
\begin{align}
 \mathscr E^+&=\mathcal L(R\mathscr E)^{\mathrm{nat}}
                        +\mathcal L\delta E_k^{\mathrm{det}}
                        +E_k^*(m,\mathscr E), \label{eq:rgnl-full-step}\\
 m^+&=L(m+m(\mathscr E)),\\
 \varepsilon^{\mathrm v,+}
       &=L^3(\varepsilon^{\mathrm v}
                  +\varepsilon_{\mathrm v}(\mathscr E)
                                      +\delta\varepsilon_k^0),\\
 \mathfrak P_{k+1}(Y,\mathscr C')
       &=\sum_{\bar X^L=LY}
           \big(\mathfrak P_k(X,\mathscr C'_L)
                          +E_k^{\mathrm{det}}(X,\mathscr C'_L)\big).
                                      \label{eq:rgnl-external-scalar-map}
\end{align}
Here $\mathfrak P_k$ is any given family of scalar
functions of the external connection $\mathscr C$.

The reblocked determinant term belongs to $K_{k+1}^x$.
Indeed the scaled arguments lie in its inverse domain,
and each summand is analytic and depends on the fine connection
only on bonds meeting $X$. These scale to bonds meeting $Y$.
There are no legs. The lattice symmetry permutes the
reblocking summands; local gauge shifts of the two connection
arguments become the corresponding real shifts on these
fine bonds, where determinant locality and gauge
invariance apply. Evenness of $E_k^d$ gives charge
conjugation, and its conjugation identity gives reality.
The pointwise bound
\eqref{eq:determinant-small-field-gain} and
\eqref{eq:polymer-reblock-sum} show
\begin{align}
 \|\mathcal L\delta E_k^{\mathrm{det}}\|_{k+1}^x
    &\le8c_{\mathrm{rb}}L^3C_dM^3e_k^{1/4}
      \le e_k^{1/4-2\varepsilon}
      \le e_{k+1}^{1/4-2\varepsilon}.
                                      \label{eq:rgnl-reblocked-determinant}
\end{align}
Here $L(\kappa-\kappa_0-1)\ge\kappa$ controls the
remaining exponential weight, and the fixed charge
condition is
$8c_{\mathrm{rb}}L^3C_dM^3e_k^{2\varepsilon}\le1$.
Restriction to $\mathscr C=0$ gives the same result
for $\mathcal LE_k^{\mathrm{det}}$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:rgnl-current-step}
Let $\varepsilon^{\mathrm v},m$ be real,
$\mathscr E\in K_k^x$, and
$(m,\mathscr E)\in\operatorname{Ball}_k^x(1)$, with
$\mathscr E=0$ at $k=0$. For $A'\in\mathrm{Dom}_{k+1}$
with arbitrary harmonic part and
$\mathscr C'\in\mathfrak X_{k+1}$, the exact density satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-exact-step}
 \mathbf T_k^x\mathscr F_k^x[\varepsilon^{\mathrm v},m,\mathscr E]
   =\mathscr F_{k+1}^x
            [\varepsilon^{\mathrm v,+},m^+,\mathscr E^+],
\end{equation}
with external scalar families $\mathfrak P_k$ and
$\mathfrak P_{k+1}$ on the respective sides.
Its integral satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-integrated-step}
 y_{k+1}^x(A';\mathscr C')
  =\int_{\mathrm{Box}_k}\dd\mu_I(\zeta)\,
        y_k^x(A_k^{\min}(A')+\mathrm{Sq}_k\zeta;\mathscr C'_L),
\end{equation}
where $y_j^x=\int\mathrm D\Psi\,\mathscr F_j^x$ with the
data and scalar family of that level.
Moreover $\mathscr E^+\in K_{k+1}^x$ and
\begin{align}
 \|\mathscr E^+\|_{k+1}^x
 &\le c_{\mathrm{fl}}L^{-1/4+2\varepsilon}\|\mathscr E\|_k^x
           +e_{k+1}^{1/4-2\varepsilon}+e_k^{1/4-6\varepsilon},
                                      \label{eq:rgnl-activity-step-bound}\\
 |m^+-Lm|
 &\le Lc_{\mathrm{fl}}e_k^{1/2}\|\mathscr E\|_k^x,
                                      \label{eq:rgnl-mass-step-bound}\\
 |\varepsilon^{\mathrm v,+}-L^3\varepsilon^{\mathrm v}|
 &\le L^3(c_{\mathrm{fl}}\|\mathscr E\|_k^x+e_k^7).
                                      \label{eq:rgnl-vacuum-step-bound}
\end{align}
At level zero this formula integrates all $192n_0$
incoming pairs of generators, with chamber measure $1/48$,
and leaves $4n_1$ outgoing pairs. Its data are
\[
 \mathscr E^+=\mathcal L\delta E_0^{\mathrm{det}}+E_0^*(m,0),
 \quad m^+=Lm,\quad
 \varepsilon^{\mathrm v,+}
                         =L^3(\varepsilon^{\mathrm v}+\delta\varepsilon_0^0).
\]
In particular
$0\le\varepsilon^{\mathrm v,+}-L^3\varepsilon^{\mathrm v}
\le L^3q^7$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the notation of Prop.~\ref{prop:rg-step-density-identity},
with $A=\mathscr A'_L$, $B=A+\mathscr C$ and
$Z=Z(1)$ the full-strength photon fluctuation.
The primitive families satisfy their exact identities
at full strength:
$H_k(1,B)=H_k(B)$, $\Gamma_k(1,B)=\Gamma_k(B)$, and
$\sum_XM_k(X,B)=b_k-D_k(B)$ for $k\ge1$.
The induced fields obey
\[
 \psi^{0,\#}=H_k^\#(B)\Psi^c,\qquad
 H_k^\#(B)\Psi^f=\psi^{0,\#}+W_k^\#(1,B).
\]
Define three evaluation homomorphisms. Let $\operatorname{ev}$
send old generators to $\psi^{0,\#}$ and fix $W$;
let $\operatorname{ev}_1$ send them to $H_k^\#(B)\Psi^f$;
for $k\ge1$, let $\operatorname{ev}_f$ additionally send
$\Psi,\bar\Psi$ to $\Psi^f,\bar\Psi^f$.
At zero take $\operatorname{ev}_f=\operatorname{ev}_1$.
These maps exist since their images are odd and have
the required antiperiodicity. They commute with the
finite coefficient integrals; $\operatorname{ev}$ also
commutes with Berezin integration, since it fixes $W$.

On the first contours $\mathcal C_rf=f(1)-f(0)$.
For $G_1$, summing the local primitives gives the
Dirac difference
$-\langle\bar\Psi,(D_k(B+Z)-D_k(B))\Psi\rangle_1$.
For $G_2,G_3$, evaluating
$\psi^\#+J_k^\#(1,B,Z)\Psi$ gives
$H_k^\#(B+Z)\Psi^f$.
The evaluations of their contour differences therefore give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgnl-first-contour-evaluation}
 \operatorname{ev}_f\sum_X\sum_{i\le3}G_i(1,X)
  =\mathrm{Act}_k^x[m',\mathscr E^r](A+Z,\mathscr C;\Psi^f)
       -\mathrm{Act}_k^x[m',\mathscr E^r](A,\mathscr C;\Psi^f).
\end{equation}
At zero the explicit first vertex gives this same
identity with the chamber pairing: $D_0(B)=D_B+\mu$
and the mass form has no connection dependence.

The reconstruction left inverse gives, on every local
first expression,
$\operatorname{ev}_1\operatorname{sub}_{Y,B}
=\operatorname{ev}_f$.
This follows on the $\Psi$ generators from $T_k(B)H_k(B)=1$
and on the old generators from their definition.
Adding $W_k^\#(1,B)$ to $\psi^\#$ in a polynomial and then
applying $\operatorname{ev}$ gives
$\operatorname{ev}_1$ applied to that polynomial.
Apply these identities to
\eqref{eq:rgnl-two-localization-sums}.
The evaluated $G_{\le3}^{\,W}$ sum is
\eqref{eq:rgnl-first-contour-evaluation}.
The evaluated polynomial contours $G_4,G_5$ give
\[
 I_k^x[m',\mathscr E^r](A,\mathscr C;\Psi^f)
                      -I_k^x[m',\mathscr E^r](A,\mathscr C;\Psi^c).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{ev}\sum_YF(Y)=V_k^x,\qquad
 \Xi_k^x
     =\exp\left\{\sum_X
                  \operatorname{ev}E_k^\#(m,\mathscr E)(X;A,\mathscr C)\right\}.
\]
The second equality is
\eqref{eq:rgnl-log-identity} evaluated by
$\operatorname{ev}$; its evaluation commutes with the
integrals as just noted.

The other remaining factor is the determinant quotient.
\eqref{eq:local-determinant-quotient} gives
\[
 \frac{\delta Z_k(B)}{\delta Z_k(0)}
      =\exp\left\{\sum_X\delta E_k^{\mathrm{det}}(X;A,\mathscr C)
                               +\sum_XE_k^{\mathrm{det}}(X,\mathscr C)\right\}.
\]
On inserted fields adjustment changes no value:
$\operatorname{ev}R\mathscr E(X)
=\operatorname{ev}(R\mathscr E)^{\mathrm{nat}}(X)$.
The equality is the telescoping reconstruction identity
for a small polymer and the definition for a large one.
Finally $\operatorname{ev}=\operatorname{ev}'S_L$,
where $\operatorname{ev}'$ inserts the outgoing fields.
Each fine polymer has exactly one outgoing reblocking
polymer. Thus the three activity sums combine into the
outgoing $\mathscr E^+$, and the two scalar external sums
combine into \eqref{eq:rgnl-external-scalar-map}.
Insert these identities in
\eqref{eq:rg-step-density-identity}. All exponents are
even and commute, so their sums give
\eqref{eq:rgnl-exact-step}, with exactly its previously
derived mass, vacuum and determinant normalization.

Integrating the outgoing generators and using
\eqref{eq:rg-step-block-marginal} gives \eqref{eq:rgnl-integrated-step}.
Prop.~\ref{prop:photon-domain-preservation} admits the whole affine
photon box; the analytic density coefficients are continuous there and
thus integrable. The external scalar is fixed and no harmonic-part
restriction is imposed.

The three terms of \eqref{eq:rgnl-full-step} have the stated real
activity spaces and norm bounds by
Prop.~\ref{prop:rg-activity-contraction},
\eqref{eq:rgnl-reblocked-determinant} and
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgnl-scaled-correction}; the first has the stronger
$3\varepsilon/2$ gain from \eqref{eq:rg-contraction-norm}.
Extraction gives the mass/vacuum bounds, using
\[
 0\le\delta\varepsilon_k^0
        \le12\exp(-p_{0,k}^2/2)\le e_k^7.
\]
At zero all incoming extracted terms vanish.
The exact algebra uses all $192n_0$ pairs with the
weight $1/48$ and integrates to the $4n_1$-pair
outgoing density. There is no removed multiplicity
or additional vacuum normalization. The displayed
zero-level formulas and bounds follow.
\end{proof}

The restriction to zero external connection commutes
with all three terms of \eqref{eq:rgnl-full-step}.
The determinant difference there becomes
$E_k^d(X,\mathscr A)-E_k^d(X,0)$, and the external scalar
map preserves $\mathfrak P_k(\cdot,0)=0$.
Thus \eqref{eq:rgnl-exact-step} and
\eqref{eq:rgnl-integrated-step} also give the step for
$\mathscr C=0$, with incoming activity $\mathscr E|_0$.

The norm estimates hold on each torus with the same fixed
constants, independently of its side and harmonic part.
Agreement of the actual outputs requires a separate argument:
we must compare the local formulas used by the primitive
systems on the different tori.


\subsection{Covers and comparison of local steps}\label{sec:rg-cover-comparison}

\subsubsection{One system and its projection}
\label{subsec:rgcov-top-system}

To compare counterterms on different tori, we project one
primitive system from a chosen top torus and identify its local
formulas wherever the cover is injective.
Fix a scale $k\ge0$, $0<\mu\le1$ and an allowed charge $e_k$.
Use the photon families \eqref{eq:photon-weakened-definitions} and the
fermion families \eqref{eq:local-coarse-families} on that torus,
taking fermion polymer decay $\kappa'=\kappa_w+\kappa_0$.
With the constants of their proved estimates, put
\begin{gather}
 \alpha_0=1/54,\qquad
 \gamma_w=\min(\gamma^F,\gamma^P),\quad \gamma^P=\gamma_P/2,\notag\\
 C^P=116C_P^{\mathrm{ph}}M^{402\alpha_0},\qquad
 C_w^{(1)}=\max\{C^F,C^P,4\exp(2\gamma_w)M^{27\alpha_0}\},\qquad
 C_w=64K_{\mathrm{pol}}C_w^{(1)}.\label{eq:rgcov-top-constants}
\end{gather}
Here $C^F,\gamma^F$ are the fermion constants at the stated polymer rate.
Impose the inverse and walk conditions of \S~\ref{sec:fermion-primitives},
\eqref{eq:photon-weakening-scale} and $\gamma_wM\ge1$.
Props.~\ref{prop:photon-weakened-bounds},
\ref{prop:weakened-polymer-propagators} and
\ref{prop:coarse-local-family-bounds}, including their component and
covariance proofs, give all primitive hypotheses of
\S~\ref{subsec:rgnl-domains} with
$(\alpha_0,\gamma_w,\kappa_w+\kappa_0;C_w^{(1)})$:
lowering a decay rate and increasing a bound preserve each estimate.
Since $64K_{\mathrm{pol}}\ge1$, the top system also obeys the weaker
$(\alpha_0,\gamma_w,\kappa_w;C_w)$ bounds used below.
At zero use the diagonal families \eqref{eq:photon-weakened-level-zero}
and \eqref{eq:local-level-zero-families}, the full chamber covariance
and the local resolvent with its factor $(1+y)^{-1}$. There is no $M_0$.
Their diagonal bounds are included above, and the block measure is
$(\eta_k^3/48)(48\eta_k^{-3})=1$.

Let $T_i=\mathbb L_k/\ell_i\Z^3$ be the two tori,
$\ell_2=J_c\ell_1$, with $J_c$ odd and $\ell_i/(LM)$ odd and at least $13$.
Write $p:T_2\to T_1$. Photon fields and parameters have period character
$\chi=1$; spinors and simultaneously translated pair fields have
$\chi(w)=(-1)^{w_1+w_2+w_3}$. Since $\chi(J_cw)=\chi(w)$, pullback
preserves these period characters. On the ordinary single-index
primitive spaces (photon, coordinate, unit and chamber indices),
it identifies smaller fields with the corresponding character subspace and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgcov-pullback-pairing}
 \|p^*f\|_\infty=\|f\|_\infty,\qquad
 \langle p^*g,p^*f\rangle_{T_2}=J_c^3\langle g,f\rangle_{T_1}.
\end{equation}
Indeed the larger fundamental set is the disjoint union of $J_c^3$
smaller ones, with cancelling characters and unchanged index weights,
including $\eta_k^3/48$ on chamber columns.

Pullback preserves the parameter polydisc and the connection domains.
For the inverse domain, pull back its decomposition $A=A_0+A_1$ and
the real gauge on each neighborhood of side $11M<\ell_1$; its local
gradient identity and all sup bounds remain unchanged. The chamber
stencils, nested block averages and transports commute with pullback.
Products and inverses preserve this identity, since
$O_2p^*=p^*O_1$ implies $O_2^{-1}p^*=p^*O_1^{-1}$ when both inverses
exist. The exact fermion operators therefore intertwine, as do the
photon operators by \eqref{eq:photon-exact-cover-consistency}.
Weighted transposes intertwine by \eqref{eq:rgcov-pullback-pairing}
and nondegeneracy of the pairings.

For a parameter family set $\widetilde O(s,A)=O_2(p^*s,p^*A)$; for
a polymer family set
\[
 \widetilde O(X,A)=\sum_{pX'=X}O_2(X',p^*A).
\]
Use the latter for $M_k(X,A)$, $k\ge1$, and $S_{k,y}(X,A)$ at every
level. These operators commute with the smaller period translations:
parameter covariance proves this in the first case, and translations
permute the polymer summands in the second. Their restriction to the
character subspace defines the projection, with kernel
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgcov-signed-image-kernel}
 O_1(\cdot)(t,t')=
 \sum_{w\in(\Z/J_c\Z)^3}\chi(w)
                    \widetilde O(\cdot)(t,t'+\ell_1w).
\end{equation}
This follows by grouping the column sum into the smaller fundamental
sets; no index weight changes. Replacing $w$ by $w+J_cv$ multiplies
both its character and its kernel by $\chi(v)$, so the summand is well
defined. Project directly from the chosen top system, without iterating
this construction through intermediate quotients.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rgcov-projected-system}
The projected system has all primitive hypotheses of
Thm.~\ref{thm:rgnl-current-step}, with
$(\alpha_0,\gamma_w,\kappa_w;C_w)$ independent of the cover degree
and scale. At full strength its operators are the exact smaller-torus
operators. At zero its local resolvent retains $(1+y)^{-1}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
At full strength intertwining gives the exact parameter operators;
the polymer sum identities give the exact polymer operators, since
each $X'$ occurs once under $X=pX'$.
There are two summations to bound. For row and column supports of
diameter at most $L$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgcov-exponential-image-sum}
 \sum_w e^{-\gamma_wd_2(t,t'+\ell_1w)}
                         \le64e^{-\gamma_wd_1(t,t')}.
\end{equation}
Choose a nearest column lift, with distance $d_1\le\ell_1/2$, and
distinct representatives realizing each larger-torus distance.
For $n=|w|_\infty\ge2$ their distance is at least
$d_1+(\ell_1-2L)(n-1)$; the $27$ representatives of norm at most one
have distance at least $d_1$. Since $\gamma_w(\ell_1-2L)\ge6$,
the quotient by $e^{-\gamma_wd_1}$ is at most
$27+\sum_{n\ge2}26n^2e^{-6(n-1)}<64$.
Projection of a covering net also proves $d_M(pX')\le d_M(X')$.
Fix the row's partition cube $\square_t$. Polymer support and
\eqref{eq:polymer-counting} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgcov-polymer-image-sum}
 \sum_{\substack{pX'=X\\X'\supseteq\square_t}}
 e^{-(\kappa_w+\kappa_0)d_M(X')}
              \le K_{\mathrm{pol}}e^{-\kappa_wd_M(X)}.
\end{equation}
The first rate pays for the image polymer and the remaining
$\kappa_0$ rate for the anchored polymer sum.

Apply these bounds to \eqref{eq:rgcov-signed-image-kernel}.
Row derivatives and short lifted differences commute with its sums.
For positive-level resolvent block norms, the pulled-back column-block
indicator is the disjoint sum of its translated indicators; the
triangle inequality and \eqref{eq:rgcov-exponential-image-sum} give
the same $64$ bound. In the polymer sum, the fixed unit or chamber row
selects $\square_t$, so \eqref{eq:rgcov-polymer-image-sum} applies.
The $H_k$ sup and short-pair estimates instead follow from the
isometric pullback of fields, with the same six short paths and
intracluster difference. These prove all kernel, block and H\"older
bounds with $C_w$. At zero $(1+y)^{-1}$ is common to every summand.

For component restrictions, lift a support and its meeting parameter
cubes together; their diameter is below $5LM<\ell_1$.
All photon parameter cubes meeting that support are linked.
Indeed their half-side is $a=M$ or $LM$,
their centers lie in $a\Z^3$, and the support diameter is less than
$a$. Thus their center differences are coordinatewise less than $3a$,
hence at most $2a$; their intersection contains a lattice site
(use a center coordinate or, for difference $2a$, its midpoint).
Fermion sites belong to one partition $M$-cube.
A lifted parameter component maps into one smaller component, since
shared sites and common faces project. Original row and column
restrictions therefore confine each image summand to that component
and allow its outside parameters and connection to be changed.
The row-vanishing conditions pass to the projection as well:
any missing cube meeting $K_c$ has a missing lift. The
parameter-independent $\mathcal B_{k,0}$ term of $\Gamma_k$ preserves
every union of partition cubes by the proof of
Prop.~\ref{prop:coarse-local-family-bounds}; it causes no
exception to these component assertions. Polymer support and local
connection dependence descend because both original indices lie in
$X'$ and bonds meeting $X'$ project to bonds meeting $X$.

Finite sums and linear pullback preserve continuity, holomorphy and
Borel resolvent dependence. Gauge and lattice actions, conjugation,
$\mathsf C$, $\varkappa$ and weighted transpose commute with pullback
and the image sums; period changes give cancelling source/target signs.
The zero-level diagonal parameter products are unchanged, since cubes
meeting their supports have unique corresponding lifts. Their bounds
are included in $C_w^{(1)}$. This verifies the remaining primitive
hypotheses without a new chamber multiplicity.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{A common local algebra}

\phantomsection\label{not:def-cover-local-algebra}
Assume now $\ell_1>(31L+16)M$, and put $d=2L+1$.
For a nonempty covering union $\widetilde X$ of partition $M$-cubes,
let $\operatorname{diam}\widetilde X$ be the largest side of its
smallest rectangular cube union. Set
\[
 N(\widetilde X)=\operatorname{box}(\widetilde X)^{\sim6d}.
\]
Call $\widetilde X$ admissible if
$\operatorname{diam}\widetilde X\le\ell_1-14dM$; a polymer is flat
if it is the image of a connected admissible lift.

\begin{lemma}\label{prop:rgcov-common-lifts}
Projection identifies all local indices and incidences in
$N(\widetilde X)$, including shortest pair lifts and their six paths.
The covering generators identify the local Grassmann algebras,
preserving degrees, bars and coefficient norms at fixed corresponding
connections and generator weights. At zero use chamber $W$ and omit
the auxiliary $\Psi$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each neighborhood side is at most $\ell_1-2dM$. Its sites satisfy,
for $w\ne0$ and $i=1,2$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgcov-lift-separation}
 |u-u'-\ell_iw|_\infty\ge2dM+\eta_k.
\end{equation}
Thus projection is injective. To lift an index or incidence, place one
support point in the chosen lift. Each other point has its prescribed
representative there, and a different period would contradict this
separation. All relevant incidences have diameter at most
$4LM<2dM$: neighbors, short pairs and paths, cube and block membership,
linked parameter cubes and coordinate supports. Short pair distances
and paths consequently agree. Independent covering generators, their
ordering signs and their measures are the same, proving the stated
coefficient-norm isometry at the stated connections and weights.
\end{proof}

For a local family, agreement means equality under this identification
whenever the two admissible connection pairs agree on
$N(\widetilde X)$. It suffices to compare a smaller connection pair
with its global pullback: coefficient locality then changes the latter
to any other admissible pair agreeing on the bonds on which the
coefficients depend. Ordinary legs
over $\widetilde X$ and admissible pair legs lie in
$\widetilde X^{\sim1}$, including the outward type-$3$ boundary pair.
Every small polymer is flat: its connected nonwrapping lift has
diameter at most $(L+3)M$, and
$(L+3)+14d<31L+16$. The small-lift result in
App.~\ref{app:polymer-geometry} and the preceding incidence
comparison give identical small-polymer sets over a fixed lifted cube,
with the same tree length, volume and intrinsic shortest cube chains.
Subpolymers, $P_0,Y'$, incompatibility and reblocking membership also
correspond: these are defined by the common cube and meeting relations.
Their reblocking closures lie in the $(L-1)$-layer enlargement, still
inside $N(\widetilde X)$.

\begin{lemma}\label{prop:rgcov-supported-rows}
Give parameter cubes in an admissible $\widetilde Y$ common values
and set the other parameters to zero on each torus. For $0\le j\le5d$,
a primitive row supported in $\widetilde Y^{\sim j}$ has columns in
$\widetilde Y^{\sim(j+2L)}$ and reads connections only on bonds
in $\widetilde Y^{\sim(j+d)}$. At corresponding connections it is
the same covering row. Likewise $M_k(\widetilde X,\cdot)$, $k\ge1$,
and $S_{k,y}(\widetilde X,\cdot)$ agree for connected
$\widetilde X\subseteq\widetilde Y$ and connections agreeing on
bonds meeting $\widetilde X$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We first justify the component restriction for a row $t$.
Write $\square(t)$ for the partition cubes meeting its support.
A parameter cube containing that support lies in
$\square(t)^{\sim2L}$: for a site use its partition cube, for a fine
bond the radius-$M$ parameter cube at an endpoint's cube center, and
for a coordinate support the radius-$LM$ parameter cube at the
$LM$-block center of one support point. In the last case its support
diameter is at most $L$, and its partition-cube centers are less than
$(3L/2+1)M\le(2L+1)M$ from that point's partition-cube center;
being separated by integer multiples of $M$, they lie within $2L$
layers. If $\square(t)^{\sim2L}$ lies in a face-component $Z_1$
of a partition-cube union $Z$, use all parameter cubes contained in
$Z$, including any whose values happen to be zero. Their component
containing the chosen cube lies in $Z_1$: its meeting partition cubes are
face-connected, since linked photon cubes share lattice sites, and
all are contained in $Z$. The original component restrictions therefore
confine the row to $Z_1$ and its connection dependence to bonds
meeting $Z_1$. The block-local term of $\Gamma_k$ preserves the same union.

Take $\widetilde B=\widetilde Y^{\sim(j+2L)}$ and its component
$\widetilde B_1$ containing the row neighborhood. The row support
meets one partition cube or two adjacent ones, so that neighborhood
is connected. Its one-layer enlargement lies in $N(\widetilde Y)$.
Separation \eqref{eq:rgcov-lift-separation} says that its image is a
component both below and in the full inverse image above: an extra
adjacent cube would have a lift in this enlargement and hence could
not belong to another period copy. The component restriction just
proved confines the row there and its connection dependence to
the one-layer enlargement, giving the two radii. The global pullback
parameters and the single-copy parameters agree in this component,
as do the connections on which these rows depend, so their top rows
coincide. In
\eqref{eq:rgcov-signed-image-kernel} any surviving column image must
belong to the same copy; separation leaves only the original column,
with sign one.

For polymer kernels, a connected $X'$ projecting onto the image of
$\widetilde X$ lies in one period copy: adjacent cubes cannot cross
the separated copies, and connectedness propagates that copy choice.
Surjectivity onto the image makes it the entire copy. In the polymer
sum and column image sum, row support selects that copy and column
support selects the original image. Local connection dependence permits replacement of the global
pullback by an admissible connection agreeing on the bonds on
which this kernel depends.
The barred row follows at $-A$ by conjugation with $\mathsf C$.
At zero the diagonal mean field has kernel $48\delta_{x,x'}$
times the common parameter product; the same argument uses the full
chamber covariance and resolvent, without an $M_0$ family.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Agreement of one step}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:rgcov-step-comparison}
Suppose the two sides at levels $k$ and $k+1$ are admissible and
satisfy $\ell_1/L>(31L+16)M$. Use the top and projected systems
above, with all primitive, domain and numerical hypotheses of
Thm.~\ref{thm:rgnl-current-step} on both tori. Let the real masses
be equal with $|m|\le w_k^{\mathrm m}$, and let the real incoming
activities $\mathscr E_i\in K_k^x(T_i)$ have
$\|\mathscr E_i\|_k^x\le w_k^{\mathrm E}$ and agree
on flat polymers, with $\mathscr E_i=0$ at $k=0$. Their extracted
mass and vacuum contributions are equal and their outgoing activities
agree on flat polymers. Agreement of incoming external scalar families on
the admitted external domains is preserved by
\eqref{eq:rgnl-external-scalar-map}. The same
conclusions hold after restriction to $\mathscr C=0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
First compare a connection pair with its global pullback.
We verify the local data of Lem.~\ref{lem:rgnl-local-calculus};
the lemma then identifies both finite localizations, their
integrals and the convergent connected logarithms.

\emph{Finite formulas and extraction.}
The coordinate map \eqref{eq:photon-central-bond-elimination} reads no
connection and stays in the two endpoint $L$-blocks. A pair-difference
row has its two endpoints and the common six paths (or outward bond),
with coefficient $d_X^{-\alpha}$; an intracluster row reads no bond.
The reconstruction formulas \eqref{eq:rg-reconstruction-two-pieces}
read $\Delta_y$, its type-$3$ bonds, and the outward boundary pair.
Their membership indicators agree by common-lift separation.
The rows of $\mathcal Q_k,\mathcal Q_k^\sharp$ read one $\Delta_y$;
the defining spin-matrix combination of $I$ and $P_L$ for
$\mathcal B_{k,y}$ reads one $L$-block. All these are identical finite
formulas on the lift, with identical column measures, hence identical
kernels. At zero use the full four-neighbor chamber $F_0$ and its
$L$-block penalty, whose kernel is $48$ times its stencil coefficient;
the first vertex \eqref{eq:rg-step-first-vertex} retains $1/96$, both
boundary transports and its outward-pair generator.

On small polymers the common constant and quadratic coefficients,
volume and measure identify \eqref{eq:rg-local-extractions}.
The common small-polymer sets over a cube then identify the mass and
vacuum sums \eqref{eq:rg-counterterm-maps}, so $m'$ is common.
The intrinsic shortest chains and all their transports identify
\eqref{eq:rg-chain-homomorphism}; thus subtraction and
\eqref{eq:rg-adjustment-definition} preserve agreement.

\emph{Determinants.}
For $k\ge1$ cycle the local determinant trace into
$\operatorname{Tr}[(\mathcal B_{k,y}\gamma_5\mathcal B_{k,y})
\mathcal Q_kS_{k,y}(X,B)\mathcal Q_k^\sharp]$.
The second factor has both unit indices in $X$, and the first stays
in their $L$-blocks, which lie in the same partition cubes.
All trace indices therefore have common lifts. The preceding finite
rows and the local polymer lemma identify every factor, and the two
spinor period signs cancel in a trace. At zero the traces
$\operatorname{Tr}[F_0S_{0,y}(X,B)]$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}[\gamma_5S_{0,y}(X,B)]$ similarly use only $X$,
with all $48$ labels and measure $1/48$.
The integrable majorants in the proof of
Prop.~\ref{prop:local-determinant-expansion} apply with the
common primitive bounds: $(b_k^2+y^2)^{-1}$ for $k\ge1$,
$(1+y)^{-1}\dd y/y$ on $[1,\infty)$ and
$(1+y)^{-1}\dd y$ on $[0,1]$ at zero.
Thus the determinant integrals agree, as do their four-term
symmetrization and subtractions at $\mathscr C$ or zero.

\emph{Read entries for the local calculus.}
Let $\widetilde U$ be connected and admissible. Give its common photon
coordinates values in the prescribed box, its contained parameter
cubes common values in their polydiscs, and all others zero.
For the photon composition $H_k^{\mathrm{ph}}(s')CC_k^{1/2}(s')\zeta$,
at a row in $\widetilde U^{\sim(1+d)}$ the supported-row lemma confines
the intermediate bonds to $\widetilde U^{\sim2d}$.
The coordinate row stays in $\widetilde U^{\sim(1+2d)}$, and the
square-root row reaches only $\widetilde U^{\sim3d}$.
All lie in $N(\widetilde U)$, so the entire composition agrees there.

Write $B_i(t)=A_i+\mathscr C_i+tZ_i(s')$.
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgnl-contour-domains} admits all these connections
for $|t|\le r_1$, as well as $A_i+tZ_i\in\widetilde R_k$.
The supported-row lemma identifies $H_k,\bar H_k,\Gamma_k$ at all
rows used by ordinary fields and admissible pair endpoints, which
are at distance at most $\eta_k\le1$ from $U_i$. It identifies every
$M_k(X,B_i(t))$, $X\subseteq U_i$. The component proof in
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgnl-finite-locality} confines the surviving
fermion columns to $U_i$ itself, including the block-local
$\mathcal B_{k,0}$ term. Thus these are polynomials in just the
identified generators. The finite pair rows give the same pair
fields; $t=0,1$ give the same $J_k^\#$ since $r_1>1$.
Incoming agreement and coefficient locality identify their values at
$(A_i+tZ_i,\mathscr C_i)$ on every $X\subseteq U_i$.
The same rows at $B_i(0)$ identify $W_k^\#$.
At zero the diagonal multiplier vanishes outside $U_i$,
its composition with $\Gamma_0$ retains the measure $1/48$, and the
common photon field identifies the vertex factors
$\exp(\pm iqZ(c,c_3))-1$; there is no $M_0$ or $\Psi$.

Common lifts preserve the subpolymers, parameter sets, $P_0,Y'$,
reconstruction memberships and incompatibility. The contour radii,
coefficient weights and ordered identity-covariance pairings agree.
Each common photon coordinate has the same normalized truncated
Gaussian law; unused coordinates and modes integrate to one.
At zero a paired chamber mode contributes $48$, the inverse of its
weight $1/48$. These verify every hypothesis of
Lem.~\ref{lem:rgnl-local-calculus}, including both localizations
and their intervening reconstruction.
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgnl-cluster-logarithm} supplies the required
weighted absolute convergence on both tori. The lemma's logarithm
clause identifies $E_k^\#$ on each flat polymer.
The omitted photon normalization is the same scalar on both tori:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgcov-box-vacuum}
 \delta\varepsilon_k^0=-(2-2L^{-3})\log\left((2\pi)^{-1/2}
             \int_{-p_{0,k}}^{p_{0,k}}e^{-z^2/2}\dd z\right).
\end{equation}

\emph{Reblocking.}
For an admissible outgoing $\widetilde U$, $L\widetilde U$ is
admissible at the incoming scale and
$N(L\widetilde U)\subset L N(\widetilde U)$.
The outgoing connection pair scales into
$\widetilde R_k^-\times\mathfrak X_k$ by
\eqref{eq:rg-scaled-domain-inclusion}; scaling and pullback commute.
Each polymer in the reblocking sum has its unique connected lift
$\widetilde X\subset L\widetilde U$. Its $LM$-closure lies in the
$(L-1)$-layer enlargement, where projection remains injective;
hence $\bar X^L=L U_i$ is equivalent to
$\overline{\widetilde X}^{\,L}=L\widetilde U$. The reblocking index
sets are therefore identical. Scaling preserves the common labels,
period signs and the rules $\psi\mapsto L^{-1}\psi$,
$\chi\mapsto L^{-1-\alpha}\chi$. Each of the three terms in
\eqref{eq:rgnl-full-step} agrees before scaling, by extraction and
adjustment, determinant comparison, and the local-calculus conclusion.
Their outgoing sums agree. The same index set and determinant
comparison identify \eqref{eq:rgnl-external-scalar-map}.
Outgoing coefficient locality extends equality from global pullbacks
to all admitted connection pairs with the stated common local lifts.
Restriction to $\mathscr C=0$ commutes with each operation and gives
the assertion for the restricted activities $\mathscr E_i|_0$. All zero-level terms were included
above with the chamber measures and the stipulated zero incoming activity.
\end{proof}

\section{The renormalization group: full trajectory}
\label{sec:assembly-rt}


We now iterate the block step and choose one bare mass for both
reference tori. The mass recursion is solved backwards and the
interaction recursion forwards, with bounds uniform in the cutoff.
The exact terminal integral retains the photon coordinates and
scalar factors needed for the subsequent partition comparison.
The terminal notation and external-density normalization are recalled
in \S\S~\ref{sec:terminal-foundations}, \ref{sec:external-response}.

\subsection{The tuned flow}\label{sec:rg-flow}

\subsubsection{Physical scales and stopping levels}
\label{subsec:rgfl-scales}

Fix $\bar m\in(0,1]$ and put
$h=L^{\lfloor\log_L(1/\bar m)\rfloor}$.
For a cutoff $N\ge0$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-physical-scales}
 \eta=L^{-N},\qquad K=N+\log_Lh,\qquad
 a_j=L^{j-N},\qquad e_j=e\sqrt{a_j},\qquad
 \mu_j=\bar m a_j.
\end{equation}
Thus $a_j$ is the physical length of one unit at
level $j$, and $a_K=h$.
At zero the charge is written $q=e\sqrt\eta$;
the fixed charge ceilings $\bar e_0,\bar e_1$ retain their
earlier meanings. A formula with variable index $j$
uses $e_j$ for the running charge, including $q$
when $j=0$.
For $0\le j\le K$ set
\[
 v_j=-\log e_j,\qquad
 r_j=\min\{L^i:i\in\N\cup\{0\},\ L^i\ge v_j^r\},
 \qquad p_j=v_j^p,\quad p_{0,j}=v_j^{p_0}.
\]
The integers $r,p,p_0$ and the constants of the
preceding estimates are fixed.
Here $r\ge2$, $L$ is odd with $L\ge13$, and $M$
is a power of $L$ with $M\ge L^2$.
We assume the hypotheses of the primitive and
step estimates, and use a ceiling
$\bar e_1\le\min(\bar e_0,1/3)$ such that, for all
$v\ge-\log \bar e_1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-scale-smallness}
 \begin{gathered}
 v\ge8,\qquad
 \left(1+\frac{3\log L}{2v}\right)^r<L,\qquad
 v^r>31L+16,\\
 (c_{\mathrm{fl}}+2)\exp(-\varepsilon v)
               \le\frac1{16}(1-L^{-\varepsilon/2}).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
In addition
$0<\varepsilon\le1/200$,
$c_{\mathrm{fl}}\ge1$,
$\bar e_0^\varepsilon\le1/4$,
$c_{\mathrm{fl}}L^{-3/8+6/200}\le1/16$, and
$L^{-5/8}\le1/4$.
The construction below applies whenever
$0<e\sqrt h\le \bar e_1$.

The physical top side and reference side are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-reference-sides}
 R_{\mathrm{top}}=hMr_K,\qquad
 R^*=R_{\mathrm{top}}/L=hL^{T^*(e)},\qquad
 T^*(e)=\log_L(Mr_K)-1.
\end{equation}
They are independent of $N$, since
$v_K=-\log(e\sqrt h)$.
The admissible physical sides for the flow are
\[
 \mathcal T(e)=\{R^*(e),R_{\mathrm{top}}(e)\}.
\]
For $R\in\mathcal T(e)$ put
$\ell_j(R)=R/a_j$,
$T_j(R)=\mathbb L_j/\ell_j(R)\Z^3$ and
$\mathfrak n_j=\log_L(\ell_j/(Mr_j))$.
The allowed unit sides are
$\mathrm{Cl}=\{\ell:\ell/(LM)\text{ is an odd integer at least }13\}$.
Their occurrence at every required scale is part
of the following arithmetic argument.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rgfl-scales}
For both $R\in\mathcal T(e)$ choose the common sufficient mesh threshold
$N_{\min}(R,e)=\max\{0,3-\log_Lh\}$. When $N\ge N_{\min}(R,e)$,
the first level with $\mathfrak n_j=0$ exists and
satisfies $1\le k_*(R)\le K$.
Its physical quantities $a_*,e_*,\mu_*,\ell_*,r_*$
are independent of $N$. For $j\le k_*(R)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-scale-ranges}
 \begin{gathered}
 \ell_j\in\mathrm{Cl},\qquad
 \ell_j\ge Mr_j,\qquad r_j\ge r_*>31L+16,\\
 v_j\ge v_*\ge v_K,\qquad
 0<e_j\le e_*\le e_K\le \bar e_1,\qquad
 0<\mu_j\le\mu_*\le\bar m h\le1 .
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
For $j<k_*(R)$ one has $\ell_j\ge LMr_j$,
$\ell_{j+1}=\ell_j/L\in\mathrm{Cl}$,
$e_{j+1}=\sqrt L e_j\le \bar e_0$ and
$0<\mu_j=\mu_{j+1}/L\le1/L$.
At the stop,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-terminal-scales}
 \ell_*=Mr_*,\qquad
 Mv_*^r\le\ell_*<LMv_*^r,\qquad
 \mu_*^{-1}<L\ell_*,\qquad e_*^2\ell_*=e^2R.
\end{equation}
The thresholds are equal on the two sides, and
$k_*(R^*)\le k_*(R_{\mathrm{top}})$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write $R=R_{\mathrm{top}}/L^p$, $p\in\{0,1\}$, and use depth $s=K-j$:
\[
 \widehat v_s=v_K+\tfrac{s}{2}\log L,\qquad
 \widehat r_s=\min\{L^i:i\ge0,\ L^i\ge\widehat v_s^r\},\qquad
 \widehat n_s(R)=s-p-\log_L(\widehat r_s/r_K).
\]
These are $v_j,r_j,\mathfrak n_j$ at that depth, with
$a_j=hL^{-s}$. Condition~\eqref{eq:rgfl-scale-smallness} gives
$\widehat r_{s+1}/\widehat r_s\in\{1,L\}$ for every $s\ge0$,
since
$\widehat v_{s+1}^r<L\widehat v_s^r\le L\widehat r_s$.
Hence $\widehat n_s$ is nondecreasing with increments zero or one.
The stronger three-depth condition at $v_K$ gives
$\widehat r_s\in\{r_K,Lr_K\}$ for $s=0,1,2,3$.
For $p=0$, the values at $s=0,1,2$ are respectively
$0$, an element of $\{0,1\}$ and an element of $\{1,2\}$.
Thus its last zero $s_*(R_{\mathrm{top}},e)$ is $0$ or $1$.
For $p=1$, the values at $s=0,1,2,3$ are
$-1$, an element of $\{-1,0\}$, an element of $\{0,1\}$ and
an element of $\{1,2\}$; its last zero is $1$ or $2$.
Monotonicity excludes every later zero in either case.

Our threshold makes $K\ge3$, so $\widehat n_K\ge1$ and the
first zero encountered as $j$ increases has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-mesh-threshold}
 N_{\min}(R,e)=\max\{0,3-\log_Lh\},\qquad
 k_*(R)=K-s_*(R,e).
\end{equation}
In particular $1\le k_*(R)\le K$.
Since $v_K=-\log(e\sqrt h)$ and both $s_*$ depend only on fixed
physical parameters, all terminal physical quantities are independent of $N$.
The two displayed depth ranges also give the stated ordering of stops.

For $j\le k_*$, depth is at least $s_*$, giving all monotone ranges;
before the stop $\mathfrak n_j\ge1$.
The rounded-power inequality and $\bar mh\in(1/L,1]$ give
\eqref{eq:rgfl-terminal-scales}, since
$\mu_*\ell_*=\bar mR\ge\bar mh>1/L$ and $e_*^2=e^2a_*$.
Moreover $r_*\ge v_*^r>31L+16>L$ implies $r_*\ge L^2$.
Thus $\ell_j/(LM)=r_jL^{\mathfrak n_j-1}$ is a positive power of the
odd integer $L$, at least $L\ge13$, proving admissibility.
The incoming mass and charge bounds follow at $j+1$.
\end{proof}

The common reference mesh threshold is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-reference-threshold}
 N_{\mathrm{ref}}(e)=N_{\min}(R^*(e),e)
                         =\max\{0,3-\log_Lh\}.
\end{equation}
The depth calculation gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-reference-stop}
 \begin{gathered}
 k_*(R^*)\in\{K-1,K-2\},\qquad
 a_*\in\{h/L,h/L^2\},\qquad r_*\in\{r_K,Lr_K\},\\
 k_{\mathrm{top}}\in\{K,K-1\},\qquad
 L^{-3}<\mu_*\le L^{-1}\quad\text{on }R^* .
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
These physical terminal values are independent of $N\ge N_{\mathrm{ref}}(e)$.

The scale proposition verifies every side, mass
and charge hypothesis of the step theorem
on $R_{\mathrm{top}}$ and its reference quotient $R^*=R_{\mathrm{top}}/L$.
At each level use the top system of
\S~\ref{subsec:rgcov-top-system}; on a smaller
torus use its projection from
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgcov-projected-system}.
These are the actual mean-field, covariance,
local resolvent and photon families constructed
earlier, with the same common estimates.
The ratio $R_{\mathrm{top}}/R$ is $1$ or the odd integer $L$,
and $k_*(R)\le k_{\mathrm{top}}$.
Thus the required top families exist whenever
a smaller-volume step is used.
Furthermore
$\ell_{j+1}(R)\ge Mr_{j+1}>(31L+16)M$;
the next-side hypothesis of the cover comparison
holds at every such step.

\subsubsection{Continuation within the mass range}
\label{subsec:rgfl-continuation}

Write the mass and activity bounds as
\[
 w_j^{\mathrm m}=e_j^{3/4-8\varepsilon},\qquad
 w_j^{\mathrm E}=e_j^{1/4-7\varepsilon}.
\]
For a real pair $(m_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm v})$,
the initial vacuum is $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm v}$,
the initial member of the mass sequence is $m_{\mathrm{in}}$,
and $E_0=\mathscr E_0=\mathfrak P_0=0$.
The variable-index notation $m_j$ includes this initial member.
The recursion is
\begin{align}
 m_{j+1}&=L(m_j+m(E_j)),&
 \varepsilon_{j+1}^{\mathrm v}
       &=L^3(\varepsilon_j^{\mathrm v}
                 +\varepsilon_{\mathrm v}(E_j)+\delta\varepsilon_j^0),
                                      \label{eq:rgfl-coupling-recursion}\\
 E_{j+1}&=\mathcal L(RE_j)^{\mathrm{nat}}
                          +\mathcal LE_j^{\mathrm{det}}+E_j^*(m_j,E_j),
                                      \label{eq:rgfl-activity-recursion}\\
 \mathscr E_{j+1}
       &=\mathcal L(R\mathscr E_j)^{\mathrm{nat}}
               +\mathcal L\delta E_j^{\mathrm{det}}
                                      +E_j^*(m_j,\mathscr E_j).
                                      \label{eq:rgfl-slot-recursion}
\end{align}
The scalar family $\mathfrak P_j$ follows
\eqref{eq:rgnl-external-scalar-map}.
In the last line the correction acts on $\mathscr E_j$ and depends
on $\mathscr C$; in \eqref{eq:rgfl-activity-recursion} it acts on
$E_j=\mathscr E_j|_0$. These are the corresponding maps proved earlier.
The trajectory exists up to a level if every preceding
$(m_j,\mathscr E_j)$ lies in $\operatorname{Ball}_j^x(4)$.
It is controlled when it exists to $k_*(R)$ and
$|m_j|\le w_j^{\mathrm m}$ throughout, including the stop.

Denote the right sides of
\eqref{eq:rgfl-activity-recursion} and \eqref{eq:rgfl-slot-recursion}
by $\Phi_j(m,E)$ and $\Phi_j^x(m,\mathscr E)$.
For $j<k_*(R)$ and two real unit-ball data put
$d_m=|m-\widetilde m|/w_j^{\mathrm m}$ and
$d_E=\|E-\widetilde E\|_j/w_j^{\mathrm E}$.
The normalized bounds are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-window-estimates}
 \begin{gathered}
 L^{-1}w_{j+1}^{\mathrm m}/w_j^{\mathrm m}
       =L^{-5/8-4\varepsilon}\le\tfrac14,\qquad
 |m(E)-m(\widetilde E)|/w_j^{\mathrm m}
                         \le c_{\mathrm{fl}}e_j^\varepsilon d_E,\\
 \|\Phi_j(m,E)\|_{j+1}/w_{j+1}^{\mathrm E}
       \le\tfrac1{16}\|E\|_j/w_j^{\mathrm E}
                                      +2e_{j+1}^\varepsilon,\\
 \|\Phi_j(m,E)-\Phi_j(\widetilde m,\widetilde E)\|_{j+1}
              /w_{j+1}^{\mathrm E}
       \le\tfrac1{16}d_E+e_{j+1}^\varepsilon(d_m+d_E).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The size bound holds also in the norm $\|\cdot\|_{j+1}^x$.
Indeed \eqref{eq:rg-counterterm-bounds} and
$K_{\mathrm{pol}}M^{-3}\le c_{\mathrm{fl}}$ give the extraction bound
because $e_j^{1/2}w_j^{\mathrm E}/w_j^{\mathrm m}=e_j^\varepsilon$.
The linear activity factor is
$c_{\mathrm{fl}}L^{-3/8+11\varepsilon/2}\le1/16$ by
\eqref{eq:rg-contraction-window}.
The two source ratios in \eqref{eq:rgnl-activity-step-bound} are
$e_{j+1}^{5\varepsilon}$ and
$L^{-1/8+3\varepsilon}e_{j+1}^\varepsilon$, each at most
$e_{j+1}^\varepsilon$.
For differences the determinant term cancels and
\eqref{eq:rgnl-coupling-Lipschitz} has the latter ratio.
These arguments include $j=0$ with $E=\widetilde E=0$, using the
chamber case of Thm.~\ref{thm:rgnl-current-step}.

The charge condition also gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-summable-charge}
 \sum_{j=0}^{k_*}(c_{\mathrm{fl}}+2)e_j^\varepsilon
             \le(c_{\mathrm{fl}}+2)e_*^\varepsilon
                          (1-L^{-\varepsilon/2})^{-1}
                                                        \le\tfrac1{16}.
\end{equation}
In particular
$c_{\mathrm{fl}}e_j^\varepsilon\le1/16$,
$2e_j^\varepsilon\le1/16$, and
$e_j\le e_j^\varepsilon\le1/48$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:rgfl-continuation}
If the recursively produced masses satisfy
$|m_i|\le w_i^{\mathrm m}$ for $i<j\le k_*(R)$,
then the trajectory is defined to $j$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-activity-bound}
 \|E_j\|_j\le\|\mathscr E_j\|_j^x
       \le\frac{32}{15}e_j^\varepsilon w_j^{\mathrm E}
       \le4e_j^{1/4-6\varepsilon}\le w_j^{\mathrm E}.
\end{equation}
The data satisfy
$E_j=\mathscr E_j|_{\mathscr C=0}$,
$\mathfrak P_j(X,0)=0$, and belong to their real
mass, vacuum and activity spaces.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put $A_i=\|\mathscr E_i\|_i^x/w_i^{\mathrm E}$.
Starting at $A_0=0$, the mass hypothesis and $A_i\le1$ admit
Thm.~\ref{thm:rgnl-current-step}. Its normalized size bound gives
\[
 A_{i+1}\le A_i/16+2e_{i+1}^\varepsilon,\qquad
 A_j\le2\sum_{i=1}^j16^{-(j-i)}e_i^\varepsilon
               \le(32/15)e_j^\varepsilon\le4e_j^\varepsilon\le1 .
\]
Thus induction admits every preceding input and proves
\eqref{eq:rgfl-activity-bound}.
The same step theorem preserves reality and restriction, which does
not increase the norm. The finite external scalar recursion
\eqref{eq:rgnl-external-scalar-map} is defined on the rescaled
external-connection domain and vanishes at zero since
$E_i^{\mathrm{det}}(X,0)=0$.
This proves the remaining assertions.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The terminal conditions and the fixed point}
\label{subsec:rgfl-fixed-point}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:rgfl-terminal-zero-pair}
On any $R\in\mathcal T(e)$ with $N\ge N_{\min}(R,e)$,
there is a real controlled pair whose
trajectory has $m_{k_*}=0$ and
$\varepsilon_{k_*}^{\mathrm v}=0$.
Along its trajectory,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-tuned-bounds}
 |m_j|\le\tfrac18w_j^{\mathrm m},\qquad
 \|E_j\|_j\le\|\mathscr E_j\|_j^x
                                  \le4e_j^{1/4-6\varepsilon},\qquad
 |\varepsilon_j^{\mathrm v}|
                          \le5c_{\mathrm{fl}}e_j^{1/4-6\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
The vacuum at every level is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-backward-vacuum}
 \varepsilon_j^{\mathrm v}
     =-\sum_{i=j}^{k_*-1}L^{-3(i-j)}
                      \big(\varepsilon_{\mathrm v}(E_i)
                                              +\delta\varepsilon_i^0\big).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We solve the mass recursion backwards from $m_t=0$ and the
activity recursion forwards from $E_0=0$ in a single product
space. On the product of the real mass coordinates and the
activity spaces $K_j$, with $\mathscr C=0$, use the norm
\[
 \|\mathbf z\|_{\mathrm{fl}}
   =\max_{0\le j\le t}
       \max\left\{|m_j|/w_j^{\mathrm m},\|E_j\|_j/w_j^{\mathrm E}\right\},
 \qquad t=k_*(R).
\]
Its closed unit subset $\mathcal B$ with $E_0=0$ is nonempty and complete.
Use the actual maps to define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-fixed-point-map}
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat m_j&=L^{-1}m_{j+1}-m(E_j)\quad(j<t),&
 \widehat m_t&=0,\\
 \widehat E_0&=0,&
 \widehat E_{j+1}&=\Phi_j(m_j,E_j)\quad(j<t).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
\eqref{eq:rgfl-window-estimates} and
\eqref{eq:rgfl-summable-charge} bound both the size on $\mathcal B$
and the Lipschitz constant of the mass coordinates by
$1/4+c_{\mathrm{fl}}e_j^\varepsilon\le5/16$,
and those of the activity coordinates by
$1/16+2e_{j+1}^\varepsilon\le1/8$.
The map therefore preserves $\mathcal B$ and contracts by $5/16$.
Banach's theorem \cite[Thm.~8]{BrightMetric2023} gives its unique
fixed point, satisfying the mass/activity recursions and $m_t=0$.

Choose its initial mass and the initial vacuum given by
\eqref{eq:rgfl-backward-vacuum} at $j=0$.
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgfl-continuation} identifies this fixed-point
sequence with the restriction of the full trajectory: inductively,
the identified mass admits the next full step, whose restriction is
the prescribed activity.
Direct substitution in the scalar recursion proves
\eqref{eq:rgfl-backward-vacuum} at every level and
$\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm v}=0$.

Put $b=1/4-6\varepsilon>0$,
$B_j=|m_j|/w_j^{\mathrm m}$ and
$V_j=|\varepsilon_j^{\mathrm v}|/e_j^b$.
Extraction, continuation and the backward scalar recursions give, for $j<t$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 B_j&\le B_{j+1}/4+1/16,\\
 V_j&\le4c_{\mathrm{fl}}+e_j^{7-b}
                      +L^{-23/8-3\varepsilon}V_{j+1}
       \le4c_{\mathrm{fl}}+1/48+V_{j+1}/16 .
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \eqref{eq:rg-counterterm-bounds} gives
$|\varepsilon_{\mathrm v}(E_j)|\le4c_{\mathrm{fl}}e_j^b$,
the step theorem gives $|\delta\varepsilon_j^0|\le e_j^7$,
and $7-b>1$, $e_j\le1/48$, $L\ge13$ give the last inequality.
Since $B_t=V_t=0$, backward induction preserves
$B_j\le1/8$ and $V_j\le5c_{\mathrm{fl}}$:
$1/32+1/16<1/8$ and
$4c_{\mathrm{fl}}+1/48+5c_{\mathrm{fl}}/16
 \le(13/3)c_{\mathrm{fl}}<5c_{\mathrm{fl}}$.
Together with continuation's activity estimate these are
\eqref{eq:rgfl-tuned-bounds}.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{One pair on the reference tori}
\label{subsec:rgfl-volume-comparison}

For $N\ge N_{\min}(R_{\mathrm{top}},e)$ define
\[
 P_N(e)=\big(m_{0,N}(e),\varepsilon_{0,N}^{\mathrm v}(e)\big)
\]
to be the pair constructed in the proof of
Thm.~\ref{thm:rgfl-terminal-zero-pair}
on the prescribed side $R_{\mathrm{top}}(e)$.
The dependence on the fixed $\bar m$ and fixed
construction parameters is suppressed.
For lower cutoffs set $m_{0,N}(e)=0$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:rgfl-common-pair}
The pair $P_N(e)$ is controlled on every
$R\in\mathcal T(e)$ with $N\ge N_{\min}(R,e)$.
Up to its stop, its mass and vacuum sequence agree
with those on the top torus; its activity and
external scalar families agree there on flat polymers.
For every such level,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-common-bounds}
 |m_j|\le\tfrac18e_j^{3/4-8\varepsilon},\qquad
 \|E_j\|_j\le\|\mathscr E_j\|_j^x
                             \le4e_j^{1/4-6\varepsilon},\qquad
 |\varepsilon_j^{\mathrm v}|
                         \le5c_{\mathrm{fl}}e_j^{1/4-6\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
The real mass sequence is independent of the side
datum and of the twist. At all $N\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-bare-mass-bound}
 |m_{0,N}(e)|\le\tfrac18q^{3/4-8\varepsilon}<\tfrac18,
                       \qquad q=eL^{-N/2}.
\end{equation}
The total lattice mass is
$\boldsymbol\mu_N=\bar m\eta+m_{0,N}(e)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For $R=R_{\mathrm{top}}$ use Thm.~\ref{thm:rgfl-terminal-zero-pair}.
For the reference torus take $R=R^*$.
The common threshold and $k_*(R)\le k_{\mathrm{top}}$ make the
top pair and primitive families available through the reference stop.
Both trajectories start with that scalar pair and zero activities.
Inductively suppose their scalar sequences agree, as do their
activity and scalar families on flat polymers, through $j<k_*(R)$.
The top mass bound $|m_j|\le w_j^{\mathrm m}/8$ and the reference
torus's own Prop.~\ref{prop:rgfl-continuation} admit its next step
with real unit-ball input.
The scale proposition supplies the domains and strict outgoing margin;
Thm.~\ref{thm:rgcov-step-comparison} identifies the extracted mass,
vacuum and box contribution, and the outgoing activity and external
scalar families on flat polymers. The scalar recursions then give the same
$m_{j+1},\varepsilon_{j+1}^{\mathrm v}$, closing the induction.
Restriction to zero preserves this agreement.
The scalar bounds are inherited from the top trajectory; the full
activity norm on the reference torus is bounded by its own continuation
estimate; agreement on flat polymers does not bound this norm. This proves \eqref{eq:rgfl-common-bounds}.

The selected top fixed-point problem depends only on $(N,e,\bar m)$
and the fixed construction, including its primitive families.
The smaller side is absent; twists are subsequent harmonic insertions
in the density, and the fixed-point map uses $\mathscr C=0$.
Thus a twist, external connection or probe does not enter the pair.
At admitted cutoffs the top initial mass bound gives
\eqref{eq:rgfl-bare-mass-bound}; at lower cutoffs the assigned mass is zero.
Both cases are real, and $q\le e\le\bar e_1\le1/3$ makes the
positive power in that bound less than one.
\end{proof}

On the reference torus, for $N\ge N_{\mathrm{ref}}(e)$,
the outputs needed at the terminal scale are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rgfl-reference-terminal-input}
 a_*\in\{h/L,h/L^2\},\qquad
 |m_*|\le\tfrac18e_*^{3/4-8\varepsilon},\qquad
 \|E_*\|_*\le\|\mathscr E_*\|_*^x
                                 \le4e_*^{1/4-6\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
The primitive estimates have the same fixed constants on every
torus and at every cutoff. We now integrate the resulting
terminal fields and compare the partition functions on the
two reference tori.


\subsection{The terminal integral representation}
\label{sec:terminal-partition}

We first put the curvature Gaussian in coordinates
adapted to all block steps. The energy splits into
the terminal photon energy and independent unit
Gaussian fluctuation coordinates. Iterating the exact
density identity in these coordinates then gives
the terminal fermion integral on the small-field set.

\subsubsection{The downward photon coordinates}
\label{subsec:term-photon-tower}

Fix a flow side and cutoff as in
Prop.~\ref{prop:rgfl-scales}. Put $k=k_*(R)$ and
$n=R/\eta=L^k\ell_*$.
On the unit torus of side $\ell_j=n/L^j$ use the
fluctuation space $V_j$ and its fixed orthonormal
basis, and the maps $A_j^{\min},\mathrm{Sq}_j$ of
the photon construction.
For a real terminal unit bond field $A$ and
$\zeta=(\zeta_j)_{j<k}$ define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-downward-recursion}
 A_k^\downarrow=A,\qquad
 A_j^\downarrow=A_j^{\min}(A_{j+1}^\downarrow)
                         +\mathrm{Sq}_j\zeta_j,\qquad j=k-1,\ldots,0 .
\end{equation}
The last field is denoted $A_0^\downarrow(A,\zeta)$.
These fields are linear in their data.

For any fine unit field $A_0$ define its block fields by
$A_j=(\mathbf Q^{(j)}A_0)^{[j]}$, where $\mathbf Q^{(j)}$
is the $j$-fold photon average on the original unit torus and
$B^{[j]}(b)=L^{j/2}B(L^jb)$.
The block-averaging/scaling identities give
$(A_{j+1})_L=\mathbf QA_j$.
Let $\mathrm{Ax}_k$ be the fields $A_0$ for which
$\tau A_j=0$ for $j<k$.
For each unit torus put
$V_{\mathrm t}=\delta C^2$, the real coclosed bond
fields with mean zero.
On the fine torus let $F_N=dC^1(n)$ with its
counting inner product and standard Gaussian
$\gamma_N$. The slice is
\[
 \mathrm{Sl}_k=\{A_0\in\mathrm{Ax}_k:A_k\in V_{\mathrm t}(T_k^0)\}.
\]

We will use the elementary cochain identities
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-unit-Hodge}
 C^1=dC^0\oplus\{\text{constant bond fields}\}\oplus\delta C^2,
       \qquad \ker d=dC^0\oplus\{\text{constant bond fields}\}.
\end{equation}
The sum is orthogonal. Indeed $dd=0$, so $dC^0$
and $\delta C^2$ are orthogonal, and their common
orthogonal complement is $\ker(d\delta+\delta d)$.
Commuting lattice differences make this operator
the scalar Laplacian in each component.
Its kernel consists of constants: the energy identity
forces every nearest-neighbor difference to vanish.
This proves \eqref{eq:term-unit-Hodge}.
Consequently $d$ is injective on $V_{\mathrm t}$ and,
on a unit torus with $\ell^3$ sites,
$\dim V_{\mathrm t}=\dim dC^1=2\ell^3-2$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:term-photon-tower}
The map $(A,\zeta)\mapsto A_0^\downarrow(A,\zeta)$
is a linear bijection from
$C^1(T_k^0)\times\prod_{j<k}V_j$ to $\mathrm{Ax}_k$.
The block fields of its image are exactly
$A_j^\downarrow$.
The coboundary is a linear bijection
$d:\mathrm{Sl}_k\to F_N$.
Thus curvature has coordinates
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-curvature-coordinates}
 \mathcal J_{\mathrm{ph}}:
 F\longmapsto(A_*;\zeta_0,\ldots,\zeta_{k-1}),\qquad
 F=dA_0^\downarrow(A_*,\zeta),
\end{equation}
where $A_*\in V_{\mathrm t}(T_k^0)$.
They satisfy the exact energy identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-tower-energy}
 \|F\|^2=\|dH_k^{\mathrm{ph}}A_*\|_2^2
                                  +\sum_{j<k}\|\zeta_j\|^2 .
\end{equation}
The image of $\gamma_N$ under
$\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ph}}$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-tower-Gaussian}
                  \dd\mathsf m_*(A_*)\prod_{j<k}\dd\mu_I(\zeta_j),
\end{equation}
where the terminal centered Gaussian on
$V_{\mathrm t}(T_k^0)$ is nondegenerate and has density
proportional to
\[
                  \exp(-\|dH_k^{\mathrm{ph}}A\|_2^2/2).
\]

There are orthonormal vectors
$\phi_{j,\Upsilon}\in F_N$ such that
$\zeta_j(\Upsilon)=\langle\phi_{j,\Upsilon},F\rangle$.
For each terminal unit plaquette $p$ there is
$\phi_p\in F_N$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-tower-row-norms}
 (dA_*)(p)=\langle\phi_p,F\rangle,\qquad \|\phi_p\|\le1.
\end{equation}
There are $3\ell_*^3$ such plaquettes, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:term-tower-coordinate-count}
 \dim V_j=(2-2L^{-3})\ell_j^3
                       \le2\ell_*^3L^{3(k-j)} .
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The one-step minimizer and fluctuation maps obey
$\mathbf QA_j^{\min}(A')=A'_L$, $\tau A_j^{\min}(A')=0$,
$\mathbf Q\mathrm{Sq}_j=0$ and $\tau\mathrm{Sq}_j=0$.
Apply $\mathbf Q$ to \eqref{eq:term-downward-recursion};
the injective scaling map then identifies the next
block field with $A_{j+1}^\downarrow$.
Starting from $A_0=A_0^\downarrow$ proves this at all
levels, including $\tau A_j=0$.
Conversely, for $A_0\in\mathrm{Ax}_k$ its difference
$A_j-A_j^{\min}(A_{j+1})$ is annihilated by $\mathbf Q$ and
$\tau$. The coordinate bijection
\eqref{eq:photon-coordinate-bijection} and the invertible
square root give exactly one $\zeta_j$ with this
difference equal to $\mathrm{Sq}_j\zeta_j$.
Downward recursion recovers $A_0$.
This proves the first bijection and its inverse.

The orthogonality
\eqref{eq:photon-block-minimizer-orthogonality}
and the Gaussian fluctuation decomposition give
at each level
\[
 \|dH_j^{\mathrm{ph}}A_j\|_2^2
       =\|dH_{j+1}^{\mathrm{ph}}A_{j+1}\|_2^2+\|\zeta_j\|^2 .
\]
Summing, and using $H_0^{\mathrm{ph}}=I$, proves
\eqref{eq:term-tower-energy}.
The dimension of the slice is
\[
 2\ell_k^3-2+\sum_{j<k}(2\ell_j^3-2\ell_{j+1}^3)
                                                    =2n^3-2=\dim F_N.
\]
If $dA_0=0$ on the slice, the energy identity forces
every $\zeta_j=0$ and $dH_k^{\mathrm{ph}}A_k=0$.
Since $\mathbf Q_kH_k^{\mathrm{ph}}=I$ and
$d\mathbf Q_k=\mathbf Q_k^{(2)}d$,
this implies $dA_k=0$.
The injectivity of $d$ on $V_{\mathrm t}$ gives
$A_k=0$, whence $A_0=0$ by the downward bijection.
Equality of dimensions therefore proves that
$d:\mathrm{Sl}_k\to F_N$ is bijective and gives
\eqref{eq:term-curvature-coordinates}.

Equip the coordinate space with the scalar product
\[
